Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NovaTel Media Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if using a landline or the button provided if joining via webcast. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NovaTel Media's Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Network Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Commercial Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I am excited to share our Q2 results, which reflect our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction. We achieved strong performance across several key areas. First, our ARPU trends exceeded expectations, driven by disciplined pricing and bundling strategies. Second, we continue to see strong adoption of our Total Connect Bundle, leading to meaningful revenue uplift and lower churn. Third, our EBITDA margins showed impressive expansion from key drivers like revenue growth and cost efficiencies. Fourth, churn rates improved across segments due to network enhancements and retention initiatives. Fifth, our enterprise and B2B growth initiatives delivered key wins and accelerated progress. Sixth, we are strategically investing in service revenue expansion across wireless, broadband, and enterprise, and finally, we are providing clear EBITDA margin guidance for the quarters ahead.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Sarah. Now, let's move on to the financial results. Our revenue for the quarter reached $15.2 billion, an increase of 5.2% compared to the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA was $5.65 billion, resulting in a margin of 37.2%. We are diligently managing our costs and optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures amounted to $2.8 billion, primarily allocated to 5G infrastructure, fiber deployment, and content acquisition.

Good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining our Q2 earnings call for NovaTel Media. As we dive into the financials, I'd like to focus on our ARPU performance, which continues to be a bright spot amid a competitive landscape. Our disciplined pricing actions and innovative bundling strategies drove robust year-over-year growth, offsetting softer subscriber adds in prepaid segments and moderating promotional intensity post our 5G nationwide rollout.

Let me start with the headline numbers. Our blended ARPU—which includes wireless postpaid, prepaid, fixed broadband, and our NovaStream video/media services—reached $58.75 in Q2, up 4.8% YoY from $56.05. This marks the third consecutive quarter of acceleration, reflecting the full-year impact of our January mid-single-digit price increases across premium tiers and the ramp-up of our Total Connect Bundle ecosystem.

Breaking it down by segment: Wireless Postpaid ARPU hit a record $52.30, +3.5% YoY or $1.77 increase. This was fueled by a 2.5 percentage point shift in mix toward our 5G Unlimited Ultimate plan, which carries a $10 premium over base unlimited due to embedded 5G Ultra Wideband access and priority data—similar to Verizon's playbook but with our edge in mmWave coverage in top-50 metros. Pricing contributed ~60% of the uplift, with the balance from 15% adoption of add-ons like our 100GB hotspot tethering bolt-on, launched in partnership with Apple for seamless iPhone 15 integration.

Prepaid ARPU was steady at $32.40, +1.2% YoY or $0.38, as we leaned into value-oriented plans to counter T-Mobile's aggressive Magenta promotions. Here, bundling with NovaStream ad-supported tiers helped stem erosion, adding ~$2 per user in cross-sell revenue without cannibalizing core mobile ARPU.

Fixed Broadband ARPU was our strongest performer at $68.20, +6.1% YoY or $3.92 increase. Fiber-to-the-home penetration now at 42% of our 18 million broadband subs drove this, with gigabit plans averaging $85/month versus $55 for legacy DOCSIS 3.1. We implemented targeted $5-7 price hikes on 70% of our non-fiber base in April, mirroring Comcast's Xfinity strategy, while waiving them for bundle qualifiers to minimize churn—resulting in just 0.8% quarterly attrition.

NovaStream Media ARPU was $14.50 standalone, but critically $22.80 when bundled—a 57% premium. YoY, this segment grew 12.4% to reflect ad-tier upgrades and our exclusive HBO Max content deal, positioning us against Disney+ bundles from Charter.

Pricing strategies were the primary engine, accounting for ~65% or $1.85 of the blended YoY uplift. We executed selective increases—averaging 4-6% on postpaid unlimited and broadband plans—while protecting affordability in prepaid and rural markets. This approach yielded minimal pushback, with net promoter scores holding at 72, thanks to proactive communications via our myNovaTel app and 85% opt-in SMS campaigns. Importantly, these hikes are sustainable; we've modeled flat pricing for H2 as we shift focus to usage-based elasticity testing on our 5G Standalone core network.

Bundling strategies amplified this by 35% of the ARPU gain or $1.00, with penetration now at 28% of our 65 million total RGU base—up from 19% YoY. Our flagship Total Connect Bundle—5G mobile + 1Gbps fiber + NovaStream Premium + smart home IoT—delivers $112/month blended ARPU, versus $92 unbundled, and boasts 1.1% quarterly churn—half the industry average per New Street Research benchmarks. We've seen 2.3 million net adds to bundles in the past year, driven by zero-rating Netflix 4K streams and parametric insurance upsells for device protection.

Regionally, performance varied thoughtfully: North America, 85% of revenue, +5.2% blended ARPU YoY, led by U.S. fiber expansions in the Sun Belt, where we're outpacing AT&T's 4.1% in similar markets per FCC data. Europe, 10%, +3.1% to €48.20 equivalent, tempered by regulatory caps in Germany but boosted by Vodafone JV synergies on 5G fixed wireless access bundles. Emerging Markets in Latin America, 5%, +7.8% to $18.50 equivalent, via prepaid-to-postpaid migrations and Claro-inspired bundles with local streaming like Claro Video.

Strategically, these trends underscore our pivot to 'ARPU-first growth' in a maturing 5G cycle. With capex peaking at 18% of revenue for Open RAN trials and edge computing for low-latency gaming bundles, we expect full-year blended ARPU growth of 4.5-5.0%, trending toward 5-6% in FY'25 as 6G R&D and AI-driven personalization—e.g., dynamic pricing via our NovaAI platform—unlock further premiums. Churn remains elite at 0.95% monthly postpaid, validating our focus over volume chasing. We're well-positioned against peers: our ARPU multiple now supports a 12x EV/EBITDA versus T-Mobile's 11x, with upside from M&A like potential Liberty Latin America tuck-ins.

Turning to service revenue growth, which rose 5.2% year-over-year to $12.5 billion, representing 78% of our total revenue mix and underscoring the resilience of our core connectivity business amid a maturing post-pandemic landscape. This growth was driven by a balanced contribution across wireless, broadband, and enterprise—despite macroeconomic headwinds like elevated churn from affordability pressures and competitive intensity in select markets.

Wireless service revenue increased 4.1% YoY to $7.8 billion. Our largest segment saw robust postpaid net additions and modest ARPU expansion. We added 452,000 postpaid phone net adds—our strongest quarterly performance since Q1 2022—bringing our total postpaid base to 58.2 million, up 1.8% YoY. This was propelled by our aggressive 5G Ultra Wideband rollout, now covering 95% of our top 100 U.S. metro markets, including full mid-band C-band deployment following our $3.2 billion FCC spectrum auction win earlier this year. ARPU ticked up 2.3% to $52.18, driven by a favorable mix shift toward premium unlimited plans bundled with our new 5G Mobile Edge Computing services, which saw 15% QoQ uptake among early adopters.

Regionally, we saw outsized growth in the Northeast and Sunbelt corridors—up 6.2% YoY in markets like New York and Florida—where population in-migration and enterprise mobility demand are tailwinds. Conversely, rural Midwest pockets lagged at +1.9%, where fixed wireless access trials are ramping to counter satellite competitors like Starlink. Churn held steady at 0.92%, bolstered by our AI-driven retention engine, which uses predictive analytics to target at-risk customers with personalized offers, reducing voluntary disconnects by 18%. Looking ahead, we expect wireless service growth to accelerate to the mid-4% range in Q4, anchored by holiday device promotions tied to our Snapdragon X Elite-powered 5G laptops.

Broadband was the star performer, surging 8.7% YoY to $3.2 billion and marking our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth. This reflects aggressive fiber investments and share gains in a market where hybrid fiber-coax peers like Comcast's Xfinity are facing capacity constraints. We reported 1.1 million revenue-generating units added, with high-speed internet subs up 4.2% to 22.4 million. Average revenue per account climbed 3.1% to $78.45, thanks to speed tiering—our 2 Gbps+ 'Gigabit Pro' tier now represents 28% of the base, up from 19% a year ago—and bundling with our streaming media services via NovaStream, our DTC platform aggregating Peacock, Paramount+, and ESPN+ content.

On the technical front, we've passed 12 million locations with fiber-to-the-premises, a 22% YoY increase, including 2.5 million new passings in the quarter through our $1.8 billion capex allocation to Open RAN deployments in partnership with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony. This is yielding 40% lower opex per node versus legacy systems. Regionally, the Southeast led with +11.3% growth, benefiting from BEAD program funding tailwinds, while California markets grew +7.9% amid cord-cutting acceleration. Enterprise broadband crossover—fixed wireless for SMBs—added 150,000 subs, mitigating headwinds from T-Mobile's FWA push. We view broadband as our highest-margin growth engine, targeting 9-10% YoY in FY24 as we hit 15 million FTTP passings.

Enterprise service revenue rounded out the triad with solid 2.9% YoY growth to $1.5 billion, navigating a bifurcated environment: strength in next-gen services offsetting declines in legacy voice and data. Contracted bookings hit a record $2.1 billion, up 14% YoY, with a 1.3x book-to-bill ratio signaling a robust pipeline. Key drivers included 5G private networks, now live for 45 Fortune 1000 clients like manufacturing giants in the auto sector, leveraging network slicing for ultra-reliable low-latency comms—think real-time robotics in Ford plants. Our SD-WAN and SASE portfolio grew 22% YoY, capturing cloud migration demand with direct AWS Direct Connect and Azure Peering integrations.

ARPU for enterprise held firm at $1,420 per site, up 1.2%, supported by cybersecurity add-ons amid rising ransomware threats—our Zero Trust platform protected 3.2 million endpoints this quarter. Regionally, EMEA delivered +5.6% growth via our Vodafone partnership for 5G Standalone core, while APAC was flat due to softer demand in China from regulatory overhangs. Legacy T1/E1 circuits declined 8%, but we're migrating 65% of those to fiber Ethernet at 2-3x margins. Strategically, we're positioning enterprise as a 20%+ EBITDA margin business by 2025 through edge computing hubs co-located with hyperscalers, targeting $500 million in incremental annual revenue from AI workload offload.

In aggregate, service revenue growth of 5.2% exceeded the Street's 4.8% consensus, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 120 bps to 42.3%, reflecting our disciplined cost controls—opex per sub down 3% via automation and 5G core efficiencies. Industry tailwinds like the FCC's 3.45 GHz CBRS expansion and Ripple Effects from Open RAN are de-risking our $18 billion multi-year capex plan, focused 60% on wireless densification and 40% on fiber. Challenges persist: promotional pricing wars with T-Mobile and Verizon could pressure ARPU, but our 5G premiumization and media bundling provide insulation. For Q4, we guide service revenue growth to 5.5-6.0% YoY, with wireless at mid-4s, broadband high-single-digits, and enterprise low-single-digits trending higher. We're confident in delivering full-year service growth north of 5%, positioning NovaTel Media as the premier integrated telco-media player in a 5G+AI era.

I'd like to dive deeper into our Enterprise and B2B segment, which continues to be a high-margin growth engine. This segment—encompassing our managed connectivity, 5G enterprise solutions, SD-WAN, SASE platforms, edge computing, and media syndication services—delivered another standout quarter. Revenue reached $2.8 billion, up 28% year-over-year and 9% quarter-over-quarter, outpacing our overall company growth and the broader industry average of around 15% as reported by Dell'Oro Group. This marks our 11th straight quarter of double-digit growth, driven by a potent mix of organic expansion, strategic wins, and tailwinds from digital transformation accelerated by hybrid work and AI adoption.

Overall progress shows enterprise ARPU climbed to $1,450 per month, a 12% YoY increase, fueled by upselling premium services like our NovaEdge AI-optimized edge platform and Zero Trust SASE bundles. Churn remains industry-leading at just 0.8% annually, well below the 1.5% peer average from Gartner data, thanks to our sticky multi-year contracts and 99.999% SLA uptime. EBITDA margins expanded to 42%, up 300 basis points YoY, reflecting the high fixed-cost leverage of our fiber-dense backbone and 5G Standalone core deployments.

Key trends: Enterprise demand for low-latency, secure connectivity has surged 35% YoY per our internal telemetry, mirroring IDC forecasts for the $150 billion global SASE market by 2027. In media services, B2B ad tech and content delivery via our NovaCDN saw 22% growth, as brands like Procter & Gamble and Unilever scale programmatic video buys amid cord-cutting pressures on traditional TV.

Key wins: North America crown jewel—a $750 million, 5-year contract with Pinnacle Financial Group. This replaces their legacy MPLS network with our fully managed 5G Private Network and SD-WAN overlay, including AI-driven traffic orchestration for their 2,500-branch footprint. Deployment is 40% complete in the Southeast, delivering 50% latency reductions and 30% OpEx savings already validated in pilots. This win positions us ahead of competitors like Lumen and AT&T in financial services, where we're capturing 18% market share per Vertical Systems.

Healthcare breakthrough: $420 million multi-year deal with HealthNet Systems. Leveraging our CBRS-based private 5G and IoT Edge suite, we're enabling real-time telemedicine and connected devices across 150 hospitals in the Midwest. Early metrics show 25% faster OR data syncs, critical for surgical robotics. This builds on our Q2 momentum and expands our healthcare vertical to $1.2 billion annualized run-rate, growing 40% YoY amid HIPAA-compliant edge AI demand.

Media synergy win: $280 million, 3-year partnership with StreamGlobal Entertainment. They're licensing our NovaCDN for low-latency OTT delivery and integrating our ad insertion tech for targeted AVOD monetization. This deal, live in Q3, is driving 15% uplift in their viewer retention and positions us as the go-to for hyperscalers like AWS Outposts integrations.

International spotlight: $350 million expansion with EuroLogistics in EMEA. Post our acquisition of FiberLink Europe, we've rolled out 400G fiber rings and SASE for their 50 DCN across Germany and the Nordics. This 5-year renewal adds $150 million in new recurring revenue from cybersecurity add-ons, tapping into the EU's NIS2 regulations mandating resilient networks.

These wins alone contribute $1.8 billion to our backlog, with 60% expected to recognize within 24 months. Our 'ConnectSphere' platform—combining 5G slicing, NVIDIA-powered edge AI, and VMware Telco Cloud integrations—is the secret sauce. We've deployed private 5G to 450 enterprise sites YTD, up 150% YoY, enabling use cases like AR/VR training for manufacturing clients akin to Verizon's Visual Edge. In media, our AI Dynamic Ad Platform uses ML to boost CPMs by 18% via contextual targeting, competing directly with The Trade Desk.

Regionally: North America, 65% of segment revenue, 32% YoY growth to $1.8 billion, led by hyperscale data center interconnects amid AI boom—our dark fiber deals with colos like Equinix are up 50%. EMEA, 20%, 25% growth to $560 million, accelerated by FiberLink synergies and UK 5G spectrum wins; we're targeting 30% share in DACH private networks. APAC/LATAM, 15%, 18% growth to $420 million, with Brazil fiber rollout and Singapore edge hubs countering currency headwinds; pipeline here is $3 billion, eyeing Indonesia's data localization push.

This isn't just growth—it's margin-accretive, strategic positioning. We're out-investing peers in capex efficiency, with 5G opex-to-capex at 1.2x versus AT&T's 1.5x, per New Street Research. M&A like FiberLink adds 15% to our European EBITDA margins. Looking forward, we see 25-30% growth in FY24, with $12 billion in qualified pipeline. This segment now represents 35% of total revenue, up from 28% last year, and is key to our 15%+ EPS CAGR target.

Before handing over, let me dive into our EBITDA margin performance, which came in at 37.2% for the quarter—up 320 basis points year-over-year from 34.0% and 110 basis points sequentially from Q2's 36.1%. This marks our strongest quarterly margin in the past five years and puts us ahead of the peer average of 35.8% as reported by S&P Global for the broader Telecom and Media sector. On a trailing 12-month basis, our Adjusted EBITDA margin now stands at 36.5%, reflecting sustained operational leverage amid a challenging macro environment.

Key drivers start with top-line contributions. Revenue grew 8% YoY to $14.2 billion, led by a 12% surge in mobile data services—fueled by our nationwide 5G Ultra Wideband rollout, which now covers 85% of our U.S. postpaid subscriber base of 112 million. ARPU expanded 4% to $58.20, driven by premium 5G plans and add-on features like our 'NovaTel Edge' unlimited high-speed data bundles, which have uptake rates exceeding 40% among new activations. In our Media segment, streaming revenues from NovaStream jumped 22% YoY to $2.1 billion, with paid subscribers hitting 28 million—a testament to hit originals and exclusive sports rights from our NBA and NFL partnerships, mirroring the content moat strategies we've seen from peers like Comcast's Peacock and Warner Bros. Discovery.

On the cost side, we've realized $450 million in sequential opex savings, expanding margins through disciplined expense management. SG&A as a percentage of revenue declined 180 basis points YoY to 18.4%, thanks to our enterprise-wide AI-driven network optimization platform—'NetOptix AI'—which has reduced churn by 25% in our wireless segment to 0.85% monthly and cut field service costs by 15% via predictive maintenance. We've also locked in multi-year vendor contracts with Nokia and Ericsson for RAN equipment at 10-12% below prior pricing, mitigating inflation pressures that have plagued peers like Verizon, whose margins contracted 50 bps in their last quarter due to higher spectrum auction amortization.

Capex efficiency is another tailwind: We deployed $2.8 billion in Q2, or 19.7% of revenue—flat YoY but shifted toward high-ROI fiber-to-the-home builds, now passing 55% of our U.S. footprint. This has boosted fixed broadband margins to 42%, up from 38% a year ago, as gigabit speeds command a $15 ARPU premium and support bundling with NovaStream for 65% household penetration. Comparatively, AT&T's fiber margins are tracking similarly at around 40%, but our open-access model in select markets is attracting wholesale partners like Google Fiber, adding $120 million in ancillary revenues.

Regionally, our U.S. operations drove 75% of the margin expansion, with EBITDA margins hitting 39.5%—bolstered by post-merger synergies from our StreamNet acquisition last year, which delivered $300 million in run-rate savings through content library consolidation and back-office redundancies. Europe, representing 15% of revenues, saw margins steady at 32%, pressured by regulatory fees in the EU's Digital Markets Act environment but offset by 5G Standalone core network launches in the UK and Germany, which improved latency by 40% and are positioning us for enterprise IoT wins. In Latin America—10% of the mix—margins dipped to 28% due to 15% FX headwinds from the weakening Brazilian real and Argentine peso, but we're countering with dollar-denominated pricing and opex cuts targeting 500 bps improvement in FY24.

Looking at trends over the past eight quarters, we've engineered a steady climb from 31.2% in Q4'21 amid peak COVID capex, through a 2022 trough of 33.5% during spectrum auction digestion—similar to T-Mobile's trajectory post-AWS 2.5GHz wins—to today's 37%+ run-rate. This 590 bps two-year expansion stems from three levers: revenue mix shift toward high-margin digital services (now 62% of total revs, up from 48%), 22% cumulative opex deflation via automation and outsourcing, and capex intensity dropping to 18-20% of revs from 24% peaks, as 5G densification matures.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on mid-teens EBITDA growth in FY24 through accelerating hybrid fiber-wireless convergence to capture the $100 billion U.S. broadband TAM; scaling ad-supported tiers on NovaStream to boost margins by 200-300 bps, à la Netflix's successful pivot; and monetizing our 1.2 petabytes of edge data via B2B analytics, targeting $500 million in new high-margin revenues. Risks remain—content inflation could pressure Media margins if linear TV ad softness persists, and potential FCC spectrum auctions may add $1-2 billion in near-term costs—but our fortress balance sheet with $8 billion in cash supports opportunistic M&A, like divesting non-core tower assets.

As we turn to our forward guidance, I'd like to dive deep into our EBITDA margin outlook, which remains a cornerstone of our financial health in this capital-intensive telecom and media landscape. For context, our trailing twelve-month EBITDA margin stands at 38.2%, up 210 basis points year-over-year, driven by disciplined cost management and accelerating 5G revenue ramps. This puts us in the upper echelon among peers like Verizon and AT&T, who are hovering around 39-41%, while European incumbents like Vodafone lag at 35-37% amid heavier regulatory headwinds.

Looking ahead, we are guiding for Q4 2024 EBITDA margins of 39.5% to 40.5%, representing a 130-230 basis point sequential expansion from Q3's 38.3%. For the full FY 2025, we expect margins to reach 40% to 42%, a 170-380 basis point improvement over FY24's projected 38.3%. This guidance embeds our confidence in sustainable profitability amid moderating capex intensity and tailwinds from our 'Network Next' transformation initiative.

Key drivers: First, revenue growth momentum—we anticipate consolidated revenue growth of 4-6% in Q4 and 5-7% for FY25, fueled by postpaid mobile ARPU expansion to $55-$57, up from $54.20 today, thanks to 5G Ultra Wideband pricing tiers and fixed wireless access penetration hitting 15% of our broadband base. In media, our NovaStream+ platform—our direct-to-consumer bundle akin to Comcast's Xfinity Stream—saw 8% YoY subscriber growth to 12 million, with ARPU uplift from ad-tiering and bundling with Paramount+ and Peacock content deals. Enterprise 5G private networks, now 20% of wireless service revenue, are scaling rapidly, mirroring T-Mobile's success but with our edge in mmWave spectrum holdings from the 2023 C-band auction.

On the cost side, opex efficiencies are the margin expander. We've realized $450 million in run-rate savings YTD through our AI-driven Network Operations Center automation, reducing field maintenance costs by 22% via predictive analytics on our 1.2 million small cells. Our Open RAN deployment—now at 25% of new sites, ahead of DISH Network's curve—is yielding 15-20% lower TCO versus traditional vendors like Ericsson and Nokia. This flows straight to EBITDA, as opex as a percentage of revenue dips to 52-53% in Q4 from 54.5% this quarter.

Capex discipline is pivotal: FY24 capex came in at 16.5% of revenue, and we're guiding FY25 to 15-16%, down from historical 18-20% peaks during our 5G buildout. Spectrum refarming in the 3.5 GHz band and CPRI-to-eCPRI migration in our fronthaul are freeing up $300 million annually, allowing us to pivot capex toward high-ROI areas like 5G-Advanced trials and fiber-to-the-x overbuilds in underserved U.S. markets. Depreciation per tower is down 8% YoY due to our asset refresh program.

Regionally, this guidance is weighted toward North America strength, where U.S. wireless margins hit 45% in Q3—bolstered by BEAD program subsidies totaling $2.2 billion for rural broadband—offsetting softer Europe at 32% amid Ofcom price caps and Iliad/Plenitude competition. In Asia-Pacific, our JV with Singtel is ramping 5G SA coverage to 85%, pushing APAC margins toward 36% by year-end, though forex headwinds from a stronger USD shave 20 bps off the guide.

Strategically, we're laser-focused on convergence plays to defend margins against disruptors like Starlink and cord-cutters. Our 'One Network' strategy integrates wireline fiber—now 40 million homes passed, targeting 50 million by 2026—with media assets, driving 2-3% incremental margin from cross-sell—think 5G mmWave bonded to our 10G PON for symmetrical gigabit services. We're also monetizing edge computing via partnerships with AWS Outposts, projecting $150 million in new FY25 EBITDA from low-latency enterprise slices for AR/VR media delivery.

Of course, risks remain: Elevated inflation could pressure vendor contracts by 50-100 bps if steel and energy costs spike; competitive intensity in FWA from Charter's Spectrum Mobile; and potential FCC spectrum auction delays. But our free cash flow guidance of $8.5-9 billion for FY25—25% FCF conversion of EBITDA—gives us ample dry powder for $4 billion in buybacks and a 4.2% dividend yield. This 40-42% FY25 EBITDA margin guide reflects the maturation of our 5G investments and a shift to growth-mode profitability. We're not just keeping pace with peers; we're setting the bar in telecom-media convergence.

Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. As we dive into our customer metrics, I'd like to spend some time on churn rate analysis, which remains a cornerstone of our profitability and long-term value creation at NovaTel Media. For context, we're reporting blended monthly churn across our postpaid mobile, fixed broadband, and streaming media segments. Our Q2 2024 blended churn came in at 1.35%, a 15 basis point improvement quarter-over-quarter from 1.50%, and a robust 25 basis point decline year-over-year from 1.60%. This marks our lowest quarterly churn in three years, underscoring the effectiveness of our retention strategies amid a competitive landscape.

Breaking it down by segment: In postpaid mobile, which represents 55% of our revenue base, churn improved to 0.98% monthly—down from 1.12% YoY. This is ahead of industry benchmarks like Verizon's reported 0.95% and AT&T's 1.05%. Fixed broadband held steady at 1.45%, benefiting from our ongoing FTTH deployments, while our streaming media unit—powered by our NovaStream+ platform—saw quarterly churn dip to 4.2% (annualized ~15%), competitive with Netflix's 4.5% and Disney+'s 5.1% amid the ongoing cord-cutting wave.

Key trends show a clear downward trajectory. We've enjoyed six consecutive quarters of sequential churn improvement, driven by a 22% YoY increase in our customer tenure average, now at 48 months across postpaid segments. However, we did see a modest uptick in prepaid mobile churn to 3.2% in Q2, up 10 bps QoQ, largely tied to macroeconomic headwinds like inflation and softening consumer spending, which echoes trends at T-Mobile and regional prepaid players in emerging markets.

Primary drivers are multifaceted. Positively, our 5G Ultra Wideband network expansion—now covering 85% of our U.S. footprint and 65% in Europe—has reduced service-related churn by 18% YoY, as measured by NPS-linked attrition. Customers on 5G plans exhibit 35% lower churn propensity, with ARPU uplift of $4.50 per user. In media, bundling NovaStream+ with mobile plans has slashed video-only churn by 28%, mirroring Comcast's Xfinity Stream success, while exclusive content deals—like our multi-year NFL streaming rights—have boosted engagement, with viewing hours up 14% and churn down 12% for sports fans.

On the flip side, competitive intensity remains a headwind. In the U.S., T-Mobile's aggressive pricing and Go5G promotions captured ~150 basis points of market share last quarter, pressuring our mid-tier plans and contributing to 20 bps of our mobile churn. Pricing fatigue drove 15% of broadband disconnects, particularly among legacy DSL customers upgrading to fiber competitors like AT&T Fiber. Economic drivers, including a 2.5% U.S. unemployment tick-up, amplified prepaid and low-ARPU streaming churn by 25 bps in Q2.

Regionally: North America, 65% of subs, best-in-class at 1.1% blended churn, down 30 bps YoY. U.S. postpaid mobile at 0.92% benefits from our Verizon-partnered MVNO expansions and Starlink fixed wireless adjuncts in rural markets, where churn fell 40 bps. Europe, 20% of subs, 1.55% churn, stable QoQ but up 10 bps YoY due to regulatory price caps in the UK and Germany, plus aggressive 5G auctions inflating capex. Vodafone merger synergies are helping here, with joint bundling reducing churn by 22%. Latin America and APAC, 15% of subs, higher at 2.1%, driven by currency devaluation in Brazil (real down 12% YoY) and intense competition from Claro and Telstra-like players. Prepaid churn hit 4.5%, but our AI-powered retention campaigns cut it 15% via personalized offers.

Technical initiatives are accelerating our churn momentum. We've rolled out AI-driven churn prediction models using machine learning on 500+ behavioral signals—usage patterns, billing history, app interactions—achieving 85% accuracy in flagging at-risk customers 30 days out. This powers proactive interventions like our "Stay Connected" program, which retained 120,000 U.S. mobiles last quarter via targeted credits and plan tweaks, delivering a 3:1 ROI. On the network side, edge computing investments with Ericsson have cut video buffering by 40% on NovaStream+, directly correlating to a 0.5 ppt churn reduction. We're also piloting zero-rating bundles with OTT partners like Paramount+ in Europe, testing 20% churn lifts.

Strategically, these trends position us well for margin expansion. Every 10 bps of churn reduction adds ~$45 million to annual EBITDA through higher customer lifetime value—now estimated at $4,200 per postpaid user, up 8% YoY. Looking forward, we guide FY2024 blended churn to 1.25-1.35%, with upside from Q1 launches of our 5G mmWave home internet in 10 new MSAs and expanded NovaStream+ ad-tier at $6.99/month. We'll continue investing in loyalty via our revamped Rewards+ ecosystem, targeting 50 bps of further improvement by year-end. Our churn discipline—rooted in superior network economics, content differentiation, and data-led retention—drives sustainable growth in a maturing industry.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you. I would like to provide an update on our network performance and expansion. We continue to enhance our 5G network, achieving wider coverage and faster speeds across 95% of major U.S. metros and key European markets. Our network reliability remains high at 99.999% uptime, and we are investing in advanced technologies like Open RAN and edge computing to further improve performance. We are also focused on optimizing our network for emerging applications like IoT, private networks, and low-latency AR/VR, with deployments now at 450 sites supporting enterprise clients.

Raj Patel: Thank you. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We saw strong growth in subscriber additions—452,000 postpaid phones and 1.1 million broadband RGUs—driven by our innovative product offerings like the Total Connect Bundle and targeted marketing campaigns.
